title: Targeting FGFR Alterations in Gastroesophageal Cancer
text:
Gastric cancer is a leading cause of cancer deaths worldwide with a median survival of approximately 6 months
for patients diagnosed with advanced disease. For some patients with gastric cancer, their tumor is driven by
genetic alterations in fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) and early clinical data shows promising results
for FGFR2-directed therapies. In this proposal, we will use innovative mouse models of FGFR2-driven gastric
cancer to test new types of enhanced FGFR2 targeting antibodies and determine how FGFR2-driven gastric
tumors become resistant to these and other FGFR2 therapeutics.

title: Regional Oncology Research Center (LLMs for Unstructured Data Extraction)
text:
Innovation in oncology is heavily dependent on identification and extraction of relevant data elements from
patient pathology reports. Current approaches require high manual effort or specialized model building which
are inefficient. We propose a multidisciplinary approach to leveraging Large Language Models (specifically
Generative Pretrained Transformers) to extract relevant patient data elements from pathology reports and
compare to results from expert-in-the-loop and a BERT model.

title: The Genetics of Development and Disease PhD Program at Columbia University Irving Medical Center
text:
(Columbia University Irving Medical Center, Genetics of Development and Disease):
This proposal outlines Genetics of Development and Disease (GDD), a focused, inter-departmental PhD training
program at Columbia University Irving Medical Center. Our mission is to train, mentor, and support young
scientists in the use of genetic approaches to address modern challenges in biomedical research. With the
support of this training grant, the GDD program will provide a cohesive, rigorous curriculum, skills-based career
development opportunities, and dedicated mentorship throughout graduate training.

title: HEAR-HEARTFELT (Identifying the risk of Hospitalizations or Emergency depARtment visits for patients with HEART Failure in managed long-term care through vErbaL communicaTion)
text:
In managed long-term care, care coordinators (i.e., registered nurses and social workers) periodically 
communicate with the patients over the telephone to ensure that they receive care congruent with the patient’s 
health needs. These verbal communications between patients with heart failure and care coordinators may
include clues on risk factors for hospitalizations and emergency department visits. With cutting-edge artificial 
intelligence techniques, this project aims to examine whether audio-recorded verbal telephone communication 
(i.e., verbal communication) can be analyzed and utilized to improve risk prediction.

title: Molecular mechanisms and functions underlying the role of Fto in mu opioid actions
text:
Mu opioids such morphine and fentanyl are potent in relieving pain, but they produce many side-effects such
as tolerance and addiction, leading to the worldwide opioid epidemic and climbing opioid overdose death. The
proposed studies aim to investigate novel molecular mechanisms and functions of mu opioid tolerance and
reward that are mediated through fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO), a mRNA demethylase.

title: Esophageal Squamous Cell Cancer Initiation and Immune Landscape Remodeling
text:
(RELEVANCE)
The proposed research is directly related to public health because understanding the genetic, molecular, and
cellular mechanisms of esophageal squamous cell cancer initiation and progression is expected to give rise to
new types of diagnoses, treatments, and preventions for esophageal squamous cell cancer. Thus, this study is
relevant to the part of NIH’s mission that pertains to fostering fundamental creative discoveries and innovative
research strategies as a basis for ultimately protecting health.

title: The role of B-cells in the anti-tumor immune response in triple negative breast cancer
text:
Breast cancer is the leading cause of death due to cancer in women and triple negative breast cancer has the
worst prognosis of all major types of breast cancer. A patient's own immune system plays an important role in
the efficacy of certain cancer treatments, such as immunotherapy. A better understanding of the role of B-cells
(a major component of the immune system) in triple negative breast cancer may lay the foundation for improved
immunotherapies or prognostic tools.

title: CHEETAH Center for the Structural Biology of HIV Infection, Restriction, and Viral Dynamics
text:
CORE NARRATIVE
This Core will provide CHEETAH Center members with advanced capabilities for synthesizing new peptides, designing
new proteins, and discovering and characterizing new factors involved in HIV-host interactions. Applications of these
advancing technologies will enable new approaches and insights into many of the problems under study in our Center.

title: The Pacific Northwest Prostate Cancer SPORE
text:
Prostate cancer (PC) is a major cause of cancer incidence and mortality in US men. This year alone 230,000
men will be diagnosed and 30,000 will die of the disease; and worldwide, the annual number of men dying from
PC is increasing. This highlights the urgent need for translational PC research to uncover the underlying
genetic and genomic factors and pathways – including environmental and social contributions - that drive PC
toward its lethal phenotype.

title: Defining molecular mechanisms by which stimulant evoked dopamine drives inflammation and neuronal dysfunction in neuroHIV
text:
An increasing number of people living with HIV use stimulants, such as Methamphetamine and
Cocaine, but the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which stimulants interact with HIV and
anti-retroviral therapy (ART) to drive neuroinflammation and promote neuronal dysfunction and
neurocognitive impairment are poorly understood. We propose to resolve this knowledge gap by
creating a consistent, translationally relevant, human cell-culture model of microglia and
dopamine neurons that can release dopamine, enabling precise evaluation of the effects of both
stimulants and stimulant-mediated dopamine release in the context of HIV and ART. Combining
this system with our existing high-throughput assays, we will define the processes by which
stimulants alter HIV infection and inflammation, identifying the genes, inflammatory pathways and
receptors associated with these changes in both microglia and neurons and determining how
these changes alter neuronal function and microglia-dopamine neuron communication.

title: A Foot in Each World: Bridging the Divide Between Clinical Research and the Mobile Apps That Support It
text: Santiago Arconada Alvarez, MS, contributes to advancing public health by bridging the gap between academic medical research science and software engineering by leading research projects with the goal of developing digital health tools through the AppHatchery program within the Georgia Clinical and Translational Science Alliance (Georgia CTSA). His work focuses on modernizing qualitative research methodologies, enhancing patient and provider education, and improving health access, ultimately enabling the translation of research into impactful clinical practices. Support from this award will further his ability to apply technical expertise to support clinical needs, advancing digital solutions that enhance mental health outcomes and reduce barriers to care.

title: The AHR-FADS3-DHA axis in Dendritic Cell limits T cell autoimmunity
text:
Autoimmune diseases are caused by the dysregulated activity of the immune system. This project uses
unique tools and clinical samples to study a novel signaling pathway that operates in dendritic cells to regulate
the immune response. This signaling pathway offers candidate targets for the treatment of immune-mediated
diseases.

title: Gut microbial interactions driving infection, persistence, and clearance in patients with antibiotic-resistant organisms and C. difficile
text: Antibiotic-resistant organisms (AROs) and Clostridioides diƯicile are major public health threats, causing over three million infections and 48,000 deaths annually in the U.S. While gut colonization by these pathogens prior to infection is common, the factors driving progression from colonization to infection remain poorly understood. This project aims to identify microbial, metabolic, and host factors that inﬂuence infection risk in patients colonized with C. diƯicile, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, and/or multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. Using a combination of large-scale clinical cohorts, genomic and metabolomic analyses, and integrative machine learning approaches, we will determine which microbial products and interactions most strongly contribute to infection risk. Longitudinal studies will further characterize pathogen persistence and clearance over time, uncovering additional potential targets for intervention. In elucidating mechanisms underlying colonization and infection transitions, this work takes the next steps in informing the development of novel strategies to prevent ARO and C. diƯicile infections.

title: Modernization of a 600 MHz NMR Spectrometer with Solid-State Cryoprobe for Structural Analysis of Macromolecular and Cellular Assemblies
text:
Michigan State University requests a sensitivity-enhancing solid-state CryoProbe and an
associated upgrade to the 600 MHz NMR magnet at the Max T. Rogers NMR Facility. This
instrument will be the first solid-state CryoProbe installed in Michigan and the broader Midwest
region, and the first worldwide specifically configured for high-sensitivity analysis of pathogenic
organisms. The instrument will transform structural investigations of complex biological systems,
including polysaccharides, membrane proteins, lipids, enzymes, amyloids, and microbial
communities such as fungi, bacteria, microbiomes, and biofilms, while also accelerating vaccine
development and drug discovery.

title: Functions and mechanisms of a subpopulation of striatal astrocytes
text:
Relevance statement
Perseverative and repetitive behaviors accompany multiple psychiatric disorders and require
cellular and molecular level understanding in order to develop novel disease modifying therapeutic
strategies. We discovered that a specific population of astrocytes in the striatum regulate neurons
to cause perseverative and repetitive behavioral phenotypes in mice. We will explore how this
happens and thus provide potentially new astrocyte and neuronal targets for therapeutic and
diagnostic strategies.

title: Single-Cell Molecular Pathway Analysis in Aging Systems via Novel Mass Cytometry Methods
text:
The parent grant is developing probes to characterize senescence in aging tissues and this
supplement allows access to imaging mass cytometry to characterize the molecular architecture
around senescent cells in aging tissues.

title: Neural Stem Cell Based Virotherapy for Malignant Glioma
text:
PROJECT 1: PROJECT NARRATIVE
 One of the major limitations of oncolytic virotherapy (OV) is poor intratumoral distribution. To overcome
this problem our group has demonstrated that neural stem cells (NSCs) can be used as a cell carrier to
enhance the delivery of a novel oncolytic adenovirus and increase the therapeutic efficacy of such combined
strategy vs. local delivery of the virus alone. In this continued renewal, we focus on establishing the safety of
repeat product administration utilizing a novel and implantable based catheter system, examine tumor
microenvironment after product administration, and validate previously identified genes implicated in OV
susceptibility as a biomarker for patient selection in a larger phase 2 clinical trial.

title: Impact of Cancer Therapy on Sperm Mutations Using Sequential Samples
text:
Mutations in sperm that are passed down to children are responsible for the majority of human genetic
diversity, as well as both common and rare diseases. Here, we will use sperm from the same individual
collected up to decades apart, including before and after cancer therapy, and a mouse model, to understand
how sperm DNA changes with cancer therapy. This work has implications for understanding the processes of
sperm mutation and for counseling cancer patients and survivors desiring fertility.

title: Genetic Mechanisms and Evolution-Renewal
text:
The goal of this interdisciplinary program is to train exceptional graduate students to become
future leaders in 21st Century genetics research. Students receive rigorous predoctoral research
training from world-leading scientists in quantitative, computational, and experimental approaches
to answer fundamental questions in molecular, statistical, and evolutionary genetics. During the
next period of proposed funding, we will train 45 new PhD scientists over 5 years to make major
breakthroughs in understanding how genetic information affects biological systems in health and
disease – essential knowledge to better diagnose, prevent, and treat a wide range of genetically-
encoded conditions.

title: Hippocampal - gustatory cortical interactions underlying formation of taste-space cognitive maps
text:
Relevance: Cognitive deficits involving memory are a common symptom of several neuropsychiatric
disorders, and the inability to associate hedonic value of food and tastes with the appropriate context is
also implicated in eating disorders. This project aims to understand mechanisms underlying neural
coordination at the network level between the sensory cortical region that mediates taste perception and
decisions, and the hippocampus which mediates formation and recall of episodic memories. This
research will enable novel insight into physiological mechanisms that govern the ability to form and recall
memories of taste experiences, and help us to develop tools for tackling cognitive deficits related to
memory and eating disorders.
